sanskrit: manīṣiṇaḥ pra bharadhvam manīṣāṁ yathā-yathā matayaḥ santi nṛṇām | indraṁ satyair erayāmā kṛtebhiḥ sa hi vīro girvaṇasyur vidānaḥ ||
english: Bring forth your wisdom, O wise ones, in accord with the thoughts that dwell in men. With true and mighty acts let us impel Indra — for he is the hero, the lover of song, the knowing one.

sanskrit: ṛtasya hi sadaso dhītir adyaut saṁ gārṣṭeyo vṛṣabho gobhir ānaṭ | ud atiṣṭhat taviṣeṇā raveṇa mahānti cit saṁ vivyācā rajāṁsi ||
english: The thought from the seat of Ṛta blazed forth; the bull, son of Gārṣṭi, roared with the cows. He rose up with his mighty war-cry and spread himself through the vast realms of space.

sanskrit: indraḥ kila śrutyā asya veda sa hi jiṣṇuḥ pathikṛt sūryāya | ān menāṁ kṛṇvann acyuto bhuvaد goḥ patir divaḥ sanajā apratītaḥ ||
english: Indra alone, it is said, knows this by hearsay; for he is the conqueror, the pathmaker for the Sun. Making the slope traversable, the unshaken one became lord of the cow, lord of heaven, ancient, unapproachable.

sanskrit: indro mahnā mahato arṇavasya vratāminād aṅgirobhir gṛṇānaḥ | purūṇi cin ni tatānā rajāṁsi dādhāra yo dharuṇaṁ satyatātā ||
english: Indra, praised by the Aṅgirases, with his greatness overthrew the vow of the great ocean. He who has stretched out the many realms upholds the firm foundation of truth and reality.

sanskrit: indro divaḥ pratimānam pṛthivyā viśvā veda savanā hanti śuṣṇam | mahīṁ cid dyām ātanot sūryeṇa cāskambha cit kambhanena skabhīyān ||
english: Indra knows the measure of heaven and earth; he slays Śuṣṇa at all the soma-pressings. He stretched out even the great sky with the Sun; the great prop himself propped it up with a prop.

sanskrit: vajreṇa hi vṛtrahā vṛtram astar adevasya śūśuvānasya māyāḥ | vi dhṛṣṇo atra dhṛṣatā jaghanthāthābhavo maghavan bāhvojāḥ ||
english: For Vṛtra-slayer smote Vṛtra with the vajra and the magic spells of that ungodly, bellowing one. There, O bold one, you slew boldly; and thus, O Maghavan, you became mighty-armed.

sanskrit: sacanta yad uṣasaḥ sūryeṇa citrām asya ketavo rām avindan | ā yan nakṣatram dadṛśe divo na punar yato nakir addhā nu veda ||
english: When the Dawns joined with the Sun, his rays found that wondrous lustre. When the asterism appeared like the sky's own light, no one truly knows whence it came again.

sanskrit: dūraṁ kila prathamā jagmur āsām indrasya yāḥ prasave sasrur āpaḥ | kva svid agraṁ kva budhna āsām āpo madhyaṁ kva vo nūnam antaḥ ||
english: Far, indeed, those foremost waters went — they that flowed forth at Indra's impulse. Where was their source, where their bottom? Where, O waters, is your middle now, where your end?

sanskrit: sṛjaḥ sindhūm̐r ahinā jagrasānām̐ ād id etāḥ pra vijigre javena | mumukṣamāṇā uta yā mumucre 'dhed etā na ramante nitiktāḥ ||
english: You released the rivers swallowed by the serpent; straightway these rushed forward with speed. Whether still seeking release or already released, these sharp-edged ones still do not rest.

sanskrit: sadhrīcīḥ sindhum uśatīr ivāyan sanāj jāra āritaḥ pūrbhid āsām | astam ā te pārthivā vasūny asme jagmuḥ sūnṛtā indra pūrvīḥ ||
english: United, yearning, like eager ones they came to the river; from of old the lover, the destroyer of strongholds, was roused for them. O Indra, the earthly riches went homeward; many gracious bounties came to us.

sanskrit: indra piba pratikāmaṁ sutasya prātaḥsāvas tava hi pūrvapītiḥ | harṣasva hantave śūra śatrūn ukthebhiṣ ṭe vīryā3 pra bravāma ||
english: O Indra, drink your fill of the pressed soma — the morning-pressing is yours as first draught. Rejoice, O hero, to smite your enemies; we proclaim your heroic deeds with hymns of praise.

sanskrit: yas te ratho manaso javīyān endra tena somapeyāya yāhi | tūyam ā te harayaḥ pra dravantu yebhir yāsi vṛṣabhi manda mānaḥ ||
english: Come with that chariot of yours, O Indra, swifter than thought, to drink the soma. Let your tawny horses run swiftly — those with whom you travel, the bulls, rejoicing.

sanskrit: haritatvā varcasā sūryasya śreṣṭhair rūpais tanvaṁ sparśayasva | asmābhir indra sakhibhir huvānaḥ sadhrīcīno mādayasvā niṣadya ||
english: Touch your body with the tawny splendour and radiance of the Sun, with the finest forms. Being invoked by us your friends, O Indra, sit down and rejoice in our company.

sanskrit: yasya tyat te mahimānam madeṣv ime mahī rodasī nāviktām | tad oka ā haribhir indra yuktaiḥ priyebhir yāhi priyam annam accha ||
english: Whose greatness in exaltation these two great worlds, Heaven and Earth, have not encompassed — come with your beloved tawny horses yoked, O Indra, to your home, toward the beloved food.

sanskrit: yasya śaśvat papivām̐ indra śatrūn anānukṛtyā raṇyā cakartha | sa te puraṁdhiṁ taviṣīm iyarti sa te madāya suta indra somaḥ ||
english: He whose enemies you have ever slain with incomparable heroic deeds in battle — he sings of your mighty power; for him, O Indra, this pressed soma is for your exhilaration.

sanskrit: idaṁ te pātraṁ sanavittam indra pibā somam enā śatakrato | pūrṇa āhāvo madirasya madhvo yaṁ viśva id abhiharyanti devāḥ ||
english: This your ancient bowl, O Indra — drink the soma with it, O you of a hundred powers. The ladle is full of the sweet inebriating drink that all the gods wholly desire.

sanskrit: vi hi tvām indra purudhā janāso hitaprayaso vṛṣabha hvayante | asmākaṁ te madhvattamānīmā bhuvan savanā teṣu harya ||
english: In many ways do the peoples call upon you, O Indra, O bull, when they have set out their offerings. Let these pressings of ours, sweetest for you, be among those you love, O lord.

sanskrit: pra ta indra pūrvyāṇi pra nūnaṁ vīryā vocam prathamā kṛtāni | satīnamanyor aśrathāyo adrim suvedanām akṛṇor brahmaṇe gām ||
english: Of you, O Indra, I now proclaim the ancient heroic deeds, the first that were done. With your fury unabated you cleft the rock and made the cow easy to win for the worshipper.

sanskrit: ni ṣu sīda gaṇapate gaṇeṣu tvām āhur vipratamaṁ kavīnām | na ṛte tvat kriyate kiṁ canāre mahām arkam maghavañ citram arca ||
english: Sit down among the hosts, O lord of hosts; they call you the most inspired of poets. Without you nothing whatsoever is accomplished from afar. O Maghavan, sing the great, wondrous hymn.

sanskrit: abhikhyā no maghavan nādhamānān sakhe bodhi vasupate sakhīnām | raṇaṁ kṛdhi raṇakṛt satyaśuṣmābhakte cid ā bhajā rāye asmān ||
english: Look down upon us suppliants, O Maghavan; be mindful, O lord of wealth, friend of friends. Make battle, O maker of battle, with your true strength — even those who share not, do grant us a share in riches.

sanskrit: tam asya dyāvāpṛthivī sacetasā viśvebhir devair anu śuṣmam āvatām | yad ait kṛṇvāno mahimānam indriyam pītvī somasya kratumām̐ avardhata ||
english: Heaven and Earth, of one mind with all the gods, assisted his energy. When he went forth making his Indra-power great, having drunk of the soma, he grew in wisdom.

sanskrit: tam asya viṣṇur mahimānam ojasāṁśuṁ dadhanvān madhuno vi rapśate | devebhir indro maghavā sayāvabhir vṛtraṁ jaghanvām̐ abhavad vareṇyaḥ ||
english: Viṣṇu, bounding forward with might, proclaims his greatness and the power of the soma-stalk. Indra, the bountiful, together with the united gods, slaying Vṛtra, became supreme.

sanskrit: vṛtreṇa yad ahinā bibhrad āyudhā samasthithā yudhaye śaṁsam āvide | viśve te atra marutaḥ saha tmanāvardha nn ugra mahimānam indriyam ||
english: When bearing weapons he stood face to face with Vṛtra the serpent to fight, making known his prowess — then all the Maruts together in their own might, O fierce one, increased your Indra-greatness.

sanskrit: jajñāna eva vy abādhata spṛdhaḥ prāpaśyad vīro abhi pauṁsyaṁ raṇam | avṛścad adrim ava sasyadas sṛjad astabhnān nākaṁ svapasyayā pṛthum ||
english: Even at birth he repelled his rivals; the hero looked forward to the manly battle. He split the rock, let the grain fall, released the waters; with his skill he propped wide the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: ād indraḥ satrā taviṣīr apatyata varīyo dyāvāpṛthivī abādhata | avābharad dhṛṣito vajram āyasaṁ śevam mitrāya varuṇāya dāśuṣe ||
english: Straightway Indra claimed all mighty powers for himself; he pushed aside the broad Heaven and Earth. The bold one brought down the iron vajra as a boon to Mitra and Varuṇa, the bountiful.

sanskrit: indrasya tatra taviṣībhyo virapśina ṛghāyato araṁhayanta manyave | vṛtraṁ yad ugro vy avṛścad ojasāpo bibhrataṁ tamasā parīvṛtam ||
english: Then, before his mighty powers — the vigorous, roaring ones — they yielded to his wrath. When the fierce one clove Vṛtra mightily with his power, the waters that had been held wrapped in darkness were released.

sanskrit: yā vīryāṇi prathamāni kartvā mahitvebhir yatamānau samīyatuḥ | dhvāntaṁ tamo 'va dadhvase hata indro mahnā pūrvahūtāv apatyata ||
english: The heroic deeds first to be done — as the two strove together with their greatnesses — when the darkness of gloom was laid low and slain, Indra leaped forth in his greatness at the first invocation.

sanskrit: viśve devāso adha vṛṣṇyāni te 'vardhayan somamatyā vacasyayā | raddhaṁ vṛtram ahim indrasya hanmanāgnir na jambhais tṛṣv annam āvayat ||
english: Then all the gods increased your manly powers with praise and with the eloquence that the soma inspires. Vṛtra the serpent who had been overcome by Indra's blow, fire separated his joints like food for the eager one.

sanskrit: bhūri dakṣebhir vacanebhir ṛkvabhiḥ sakhyebhiḥ sakhyāni pra vocata | indro dhuniṁ ca cumuriṁ ca dambhayan śraddhāmanasyā śṛṇute dabhītaye ||
english: With many powers, with eloquent verses, with friendship proclaim the friendship. Indra, who deceived Dhuṇi and Cumuri, listens with trusting heart to Dabhīti.

sanskrit: tvam purūṇy ā bharā svaśvyā yebhir maṁsai nivacananāni śaṁsan | sugebhir viśvā duritā tarema vido ṣu ṇa urvi yā gādham adya ||
english: Bring us many goods with good horses, whereby, reciting the proper utterances, you may approve. May we pass through all difficulties by easy paths; find for us today the wide shallow ford.

sanskrit: gharmā samantā trivṛtaṁ vy āpatus tayor juṣṭim mātariśvā jagāma | divas payo didhiṣāṇā aveṣan vidur devāḥ sahasāmānam arkam ||
english: The two hot milk-vessels spread on all sides the threefold; Mātariśvan came to take pleasure in them. The gods, seeking the milk of heaven, found the hymn mighty with its thousand.

sanskrit: tisro deṣṭrāya nirṛtīr upāsate dīrghaśruto vi hi jānanti vahnavayaḥ | tāsāṁ ni cikyuḥ kavayo nidānam pareṣu yā guhyeṣu vrateṣu ||
english: The three Nirṛtis wait upon the guardian; the priests know them who have heard from afar. The sages have discerned their source — those that are in the secret vows of the higher ones.

sanskrit: catuṣkapardā yuvatir supeśā ghṛtapratīkā vayunāni vaste | tasyāṁ suparṇā vṛṣaṇā ni ṣedatur yatra devā dadhire bhāgadheyam ||
english: The young woman of four braids, beautifully adorned, wears before her face ghee and the ordinances. In her two strong eagles settled — there where the gods established their portions.

sanskrit: ekaḥ suparṇaḥ sa samudram ā viveśa sa idaṁ viśvaṁ bhuvanaṁ vi caṣṭe | tam pākena manasāpaśyam antitas tam mātā reḻhi sa u reḻhi mātaram ||
english: One eagle entered the ocean; he surveys this entire world. I saw him with a simple mind from nearby — the mother licks him, and he licks the mother.

sanskrit: suparṇaṁ viprāḥ kavayo vocabhir ekaṁ santam bahudhā kalpayanti | chandāṁsi ca dadhato adhvareṣu grahāṇ somasya mimate dvādaśa ||
english: The inspired poets speak of the one eagle with their words, and fashion him in many ways. They establish the metres at the sacrifices and measure the twelve soma-cups.

sanskrit: ṣaṭtriṁśām̐ś ca caturaḥ kalpayantaś chandāṁsi ca dadhata ādvādaśam | yajñaṁ vimāya kavayo manīṣa ṛksāmābhyāṁ pra rathaṁ vartayanti ||
english: Fashioning thirty-six plus four, and establishing the metres up to twelve — the sages measuring out the sacrifice in their wisdom drive the chariot forward with Ṛc and Sāman.

sanskrit: caturdaśānye mahimāno asya taṁ dhīrā vācā pra ṇayanti sapta | āpnānaṁ tīrthaṁ ka iha pra vocad yena pathā prapibante sutasya ||
english: Fourteen are the greatnesses of this one; the seven wise ones guide him with speech. Who here would declare the far-reaching ford, by which path they drink up the pressed soma?

sanskrit: sahasradhā pañcadaśāny ukthā yāvad dyāvāpṛthivī tāvad it tat | sahasradhā mahimānaḥ sahasraṁ yāvad brahma viṣṭhitaṁ tāvatī vāk ||
english: The fifteen praises in a thousandfold — as far as Heaven and Earth extend, so far is that. Thousandfold the greatnesses, a thousand — as far as brahman is spread, so great is speech.

sanskrit: kaś chandasāṁ yogam ā veda dhīraḥ ko dhiṣṇyām prati vācam papāda | kam ṛtvijām aṣṭamaṁ śūram āhur harī indrasya ni cikāya kaḥ svit ||
english: What wise one knows the yoking of the metres? Who has attained the word directed to the bright one? Who, they say, is the eighth heroic priest? Who really has discerned the two tawny horses of Indra?

sanskrit: bhūmyā antam pary eke caranti rathasya dhūrṣu yuktāso asthuḥ | śramasya dāyaṁ vi bhajanti ebhyo yadā yamo bhavati harmye hitaḥ ||
english: Some roam about the ends of the earth; they stand on the shafts of the chariot, yoked. Among these they distribute the share of fatigue when Yama is placed in the dwelling.

sanskrit: citra ic chiśos taruṇasya vakṣatho na yo mātarāv apyeti dhātave | anūdhā yadi jījanad adhā ca nu vavakṣa sadyo mahi dūtyam̐ caran ||
english: Wondrous indeed is the growth of this young child who does not go to his two mothers to suckle. If he was born uncollected, yet straightway he grew; running his great messenger's course at once.

sanskrit: agnir ha nāma dhāyi dann apatstamaḥ saṁ yo vanā yuvate bhasmanā datā | abhipramurā juhvā svadhvara ino na prothamāno yavase vṛṣā ||
english: Agni has been established by name, the most eager at giving — he who binds the forests together with his tooth of ash. Sweeping forward with his tongue in perfect sacrifice, like a bull snorting over fodder.

sanskrit: taṁ vo viṁ na druṣadaṁ devam andhasa indum prothamtam pravapantam arṇavam | āsā vahniṁ na śociṣā virapśinam mahivrataṁ na sarajantam adhvanaḥ ||
english: Him — the divine bird who pecks at the wood, the drop of soma snorting and pouring forth his flood — him, blazing like a carrier-priest with his flame, of mighty vow, like one whose rays run along the paths.

sanskrit: vi yasya te jrayasānasyājara dhakṣor na vātāḥ pari santy acyutāḥ | ā raṇvāso yuyudhayo na satvanam tritaṁ naśanta pra śiṣanta iṣṭaye ||
english: Of your ageless, glowing advance, the unshaken winds are not around like those of a burning-arrow. The eager ones, like eager fighters, attain Trita as their guide and go forward for seeking.

sanskrit: sa id agniḥ kaṇvatamaḥ kaṇvasakho 'ryaḥ parasyāntarasya taruṣaḥ | agniḥ pātu gṛṇato agniḥ sūrīn agnir dadātu teṣām avo naḥ ||
english: He is indeed the Agni most dear to the Kaṇvas, friend of the Kaṇvas, the noble overcoming lord of the utmost interior. May Agni protect the singers, may Agni protect the patrons, may Agni grant us their favour.

sanskrit: vājintamāya sahyase supitrya tṛṣu cyavāno anu jātavedase | anuddre cid yo dhṛṣatā varaṁ sate mahintamāya dhanvaned aviṣyate ||
english: For the most prize-winning, the conquerable, of good father — for Jātavedas restless and stirred — even he who boldly claims the boon of the waterless one, for the most exalted, who stretches his bow, seeking to shoot.

sanskrit: evāgnir martaiḥ saha sūribhir vasuḥ ṣṭave sahasaḥ sūnaro nṛbhiḥ | mitrāso na ye sudhitā ṛtāyavo dyāvo na dyumnair abhi santi mānuṣān ||
english: Thus Agni, the good one, son of strength, is praised along with mortal patron-lords and men — like allies who are well-established and devoted to Ṛta; like bright heavens they are over men with their brilliance.

sanskrit: ūrjo napāt sahasāvann iti tvopastu tasya vandate vṛṣā vāk | tvāṁ stoṣāma tvayā suvīrā drāghīya āyuḥ prataram dadhānāḥ ||
english: Grandson of Strength, O you mighty with power — so speech, the bull, praises you being worshipped. We will laud you; with you may we be rich in heroes, establishing ever longer life to extend further.

sanskrit: iti tvāgne vṛṣṭihavyasya putrā upastutāsa ṛṣayo 'vocan | tām̐ś ca pāhi gṛṇataś ca sūrīn vaṣaḍ vaṣaḷ ity ūrdhvāso anakṣan namo nama ity ūrdhvāso anakṣan ||
english: Thus, O Agni, the sons of Vṛṣṭihavya, the ṛṣis, have spoken in their praise. Protect both them and the patron-lords who hymn you — they reached upward with 'vaṣaṭ vaṣaṭ', they reached upward with 'namo namaḥ'.

sanskrit: pibā somam mahata indriyāya pibā vṛtrāya hantave śaviṣṭha | piba rāye śavase hūyamānaḥ piba madhvas tṛpad indrā vṛṣasva ||
english: Drink the soma for great Indra-power, drink, O mightiest, to slay Vṛtra. Being invoked, drink for wealth and strength; drink the sweet draught, O Indra, be satisfied and rain down blessings.

sanskrit: asya piba kṣumataḥ prasthitasya indra somasya varam ā sutasya | svastidā manasā mādayasvārvācīno revate saubhagāya ||
english: Drink of this, of the abundant, the forthcoming — drink, O Indra, the choicest of the pressed soma. With a well-being-granting mind rejoice, turning toward prosperity for the sake of good fortune.

sanskrit: mamattu tvā divyaḥ soma indra mamattu yaḥ sūyate pārthiveṣu | mamattu yena varivaś cakartha mamattu yena niriṇāsi śatrūn ||
english: May the heavenly soma delight you, O Indra; may that which is pressed on earth delight you. May that whereby you made abundance delight you; may that whereby you destroy enemies delight you.

sanskrit: ā dvibarhā amino yātv indro vṛṣā haribhyāṁ pariṣiktam andhaḥ | gavy ā sutasya prabhṛtasya madhvaḥ satrā khedām aruśahā vṛṣasva ||
english: Let Indra of twofold might, the bull, come eagerly to the soma poured out with his two tawny horses. In the bowl of the pressed and offered sweet juice, rain benefits all at once, O friend of the red cows.

sanskrit: ni tigmāni bhrāśayan bhrāśyāṇy ava sthirā tanuhi yātujūnāḥ | ugrāya te saho balaṁ dadāmi pratītyā śatrūn vigadeṣu vṛśca ||
english: Sending the sharp and glittering weapons flashing down, make firm the power of those sped by sorcerers. I give you strength and might against the fierce foe; in the retreats hack the enemies to pieces.

sanskrit: vy arya indra tanuhi śravāṁsy ojaḥ sthireva dhvanano 'bhimātīḥ | asmadriyag vāvṛdhānaḥ sahobhir anibhṛṣṭas tanvaṁ vāvṛdhasva ||
english: O Indra, spread widely your glories; stretch your strength like a taut bowstring against the attackers. Growing in power on our side, unstoppable, do you yourself grow strong in body.

sanskrit: idaṁ havir maghavan tubhyaṁ rātam prati samrāḷ ahṛṇāno gṛbhāya | tubhyaṁ suto maghavan tubhyam pakvo 'ddhīndra piba ca prasthitasya ||
english: This oblation is given to you, O Maghavan; accept it, O universal king, without disdain. For you is the soma pressed, for you it is ripened, O Maghavan — eat and drink, O Indra, of the forthcoming offering.

sanskrit: addhīd indra prasthite imā havīṁṣi cano dadhiṣva pacatotha somam | prayasvantaḥ prati haryāmasi tvā satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ ||
english: Indeed eat, O Indra, these oblations that are set forth; take pleasure in them and cook the soma. Offering gifts, we are eager to win your favour; may the desires of the sacrificer be fulfilled.

sanskrit: prendrāgnibhyāṁ suvacasyām iyarmi sindhāv iva prerayan nāvam arkaiḥ | ayā iva pari caranti devā ye asmabhyaṁ dhanadā udbhidaś ca ||
english: I send forth my eloquent praise to Indra and Agni, driving it like a boat on the river with hymns. Like spokes the gods go around — those who give wealth to us and are givers of discoveries.

sanskrit: na vā u devāḥ kṣudham id vadhaṁ dadur utāśitam upa gacchanti mṛtyavaḥ | uto rayiḥ pṛṇato nopa dasyaty utāpṛṇan marḍitāraṁ na vindate ||
english: Verily the gods have not decreed that hunger alone shall be death; even though a man is full, death can still reach him. Yet the wealth of one who gives does not diminish, and the one who gives not finds no comforter.

sanskrit: ya ādhāya cakamānāya pitvo 'nnavān san raphitāyopajagmuṣe | sthiram manaḥ kṛṇute sevate puroto cit sa marḍitāraṁ na vindate ||
english: He who, having food, hardens his heart toward the needy person, hungry and wretched who has come to him — though he cultivated him before, he finds no comforter.

sanskrit: sa id bhojo yo gṛhave dadāty annak āmāya carate kṛśāya | aram asmai bhavati yāmahūtā utāpariṣu kṛṇute sakhāyam ||
english: He indeed is the true enjoyer who gives to the wandering indigent, to the hungry and lean. He becomes fit for the call-to-aid, and even in future things he makes a friend.

sanskrit: na sa sakhā yo na dadāti sakhye sacābhuve sacamānāya pitvaḥ | apāsmāt preyān na tad oko asti pṛṇantam anyam araṇaṁ cid icchet ||
english: He is no friend who gives nothing to his friend, his companion who goes along with him — one should depart from such a one; there is no dwelling with him; let one seek another who gives, even if a stranger.

sanskrit: pṛṇīyād in nādhamānāya tavyān drāghīyāṁsam anu paśyeta panthām | o hi vartante rathyeva cakrāny am-anyam upa tiṣṭhanta rāyaḥ ||
english: The stronger man should give to the supplicant; let him look ahead to the longer road. For riches roll around like chariot wheels; they come to one man after another.

sanskrit: mogham annaṁ vindate apracetāḥ satyam bravīmi vadha it sa tasya | nāryamaṇam puṣyati no sakhāyaṁ kevalāgho bhavati kevalādī ||
english: The foolish man gets food in vain — I speak truth — that is his death. He neither nourishes Aryaman nor a friend; he who eats alone, his sin is his alone.

sanskrit: kṛṣann it phāla āśitaṁ kṛṇoti yann adhvānam apa vṛṅkte caritaiḥ | vadan brahmāvadato vanīyān pṛṇann āpir apṛṇantam abhi ṣyāt ||
english: The ploughshare ploughing brings reward; one who goes the road gains advantage through his journeys. The speaking Brahmin surpasses the one who speaks not; the giver who is an ally excels the non-giver.

sanskrit: ekapād bhūyo dvipado vi cakrame dvipāt tripādam abhy eti paścāt | catuṣpād eti dvipedām abhisvare sampaśyan paṅktīr upatiṣṭhamānaḥ ||
english: One-footed surpasses two-footed in many ways; the two-footed approaches the three-footed from behind. Four-footed comes at the call of the two-footed, seeing the ranks, standing by.

sanskrit: samau cid dhastau na samaṁ viviṣṭaḥ sammātarā cin na samaṁ duhāte | yamayoś cin na samā vīryāṇi jñātī cit santau na samaṁ pṛṇītaḥ ||
english: Even two equal hands do not produce equally; even two identical twin cows do not give the same milk. Even twins are not equal in their powers; even two kinsmen do not give equally.

sanskrit: agne haṁsi ny atriṇaṁ dīdyan martyeṣv ā | sve kṣaye śucivrata ||
english: O Agni, shining brilliantly, you slay the devourer among mortals, in your own home, O you of pure ordinance.

sanskrit: ut tiṣṭhasi svāhuto ghṛtāni prati modase | yat tvā srucaḥ samasthiran ||
english: Well-kindled, you rise up and rejoice at the ghee when the ladles are set around you.

sanskrit: sa āhuto vi rocate 'gnir īḷenyo girā | srucā pratīkam ajyate ||
english: Summoned, Agni, who is to be praised with song, shines forth; his face is anointed with the ladle.

sanskrit: ghṛtenāgniḥ sam ajyate madhupratīka āhutaḥ | rocamāno vibhāvasuḥ ||
english: Agni is anointed with ghee, honey-faced, when oblations are given; he shines forth, rich in light.

sanskrit: jaramāṇaḥ sam idhyase devebhyo havyavāhana | taṁ tvā havanta martyāḥ ||
english: As you blaze, growing old in your brightness, O carrier of oblations to the gods, mortals call upon you.

sanskrit: tam martā amartyaṁ ghṛtenāgniṁ saparyata | adābhyaṁ gṛhapa tim ||
english: Mortals tend him, the immortal Agni, with ghee — the inviolable lord of the house.

sanskrit: adābhyena śociṣāgne rakṣas tvaṁ daha | gopā ṛtasya dīdihi ||
english: With your inviolable flame, O Agni, burn the Rakṣas; shine forth as guardian of Ṛta.

sanskrit: sa tvam agne pratīkena praty oṣa yātudhānyaḥ | urukṣayeṣu dīdyat ||
english: You, O Agni, with your countenance burn back the sorceresses; shine forth in your wide dwelling.

sanskrit: taṁ tvā gīrbhir urukṣayā havyavāhaṁ sam īdhire | yajiṣṭham mānuṣe jane ||
english: Him you, the carrier of oblations, dweller in wide spaces, the most worthy of sacrifice among the human folk, they have kindled with songs.

sanskrit: iti vā iti me mano gām aśvaṁ sanuyām iti | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: So indeed is my mind: 'I would win a cow, I would win a horse' — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: pra vātā iva dodhatā un mā pītā ayaṁsata | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: Like rushing winds, the draughts I have drunk have lifted me up — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: un mā pītā ayaṁsata ratham aśvā ivāśavaḥ | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: The draughts have lifted me up, like swift horses a chariot — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: upa mā matir asthita vāśrā putram iva priyam | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: Inspiration has come to me like a lowing cow to her beloved calf — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: ahaṁ taṣṭeva vanduram pary acāmi hṛdā matim | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: Like a carpenter rounding a chariot-body, I shape my thought in my heart — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: nahi me akṣipac canācchāntsu pañca kṛṣṭayaḥ | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: The five peoples have not pleased me even a little — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: nahi me rodasī ubhe anyam pakṣaṁ cana prati | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: Not even both the worlds, Heaven and Earth, equal even one of my wings — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: abhi dyām mahinā bhuvaṁ abhī mām pṛthivīm mahīm | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: In my greatness I have surpassed the sky; I have surpassed this great Earth — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: hantāham pṛthivīm imāṁ ni dadhānīha ve ha vā | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: Well then! Shall I set down this Earth here or there? — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: oṣam it pṛthivīm ahaṁ jaṅghanānīha ve ha vā | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: I shall strike the Earth to a cinder, here or there — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: divi me anyaḥ pakṣo 'dho anyam acīkṛṣam | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: One of my wings is in heaven; I have dragged the other one down below — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: aham asmi mahāmaho 'bhinabhyam udīṣitaḥ | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: I am the greatest of the great, raised up to the very clouds — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: gṛho yāmy araṁkṛto devebhyo havyavāhanaḥ | kuvit somasyāpām iti ||
english: I go home, well-equipped as the bearer of oblations to the gods — have I drunk of the soma?

sanskrit: tad id āsa bhuvanēṣu jyeṣṭhaṁ yato jajña ugras tveṣanṛmṇaḥ | sadyo jajñāno ni riṇāti śatrūn anu yaṁ viśve madanty ūmāḥ ||
english: That was the greatest thing in the worlds: from it was born the fierce one of dazzling might. As soon as born he destroys enemies; all his helpers rejoice after him.

sanskrit: vāvṛdhānaḥ śavasā bhūryojāḥ śatrur dāsāya bhiyasam dadhāti | avyanac ca vyanac ca sasni saṁ te navanta prabhṛtā madeṣu ||
english: Growing in power, of many energies, he plants terror in the heart of the Dāsa enemy. Both the unshot and the shot arrow he won; your offered gifts are praised in the exaltations.

sanskrit: tve kratuṁ api vṛñjanti viśve dvir yad ete trir bhavanty ūmāḥ | svādoḥ svādīyaḥ svādunā sṛjā sam adaḥ su madhu madhunābhi yodhīḥ ||
english: All fold their purpose into you when these helpers become twice and thrice more. Sweeter than sweet, mix the sweet together; fight that sweetness indeed with the honey of honey.

sanskrit: iti cid dhi tvā dhanā jayantam made-made anumadanti viprāḥ | ojīyo dhṛṣṇo sthiram ā tanuṣvā mā tvā dabhan yātudhānā durevāḥ ||
english: For thus the inspired ones exult after you, winning riches, exaltation by exaltation. Stretch yourself firm and mightier, O bold one; may the ill-doing sorcerers not deceive you.

sanskrit: tvayā vayaṁ śāśadmahe raṇeṣu prapaśyanto yudhenyāni bhūri | codayāmi ta āyudhā vacobhiḥ saṁ te śiśāmi brahmaṇā vayāṁsi ||
english: With your help we have prevailed in battles, beholding many things worth fighting for. I urge your weapons with my words; with prayer I sharpen your powers.

sanskrit: stuṣeyyam puruvarpasam ṛbhvam inatamaṁ āptyam āptyānām | ā darṣate śavasā sapta dānūn pra sākṣate pratimānāni bhūri ||
english: I would praise the one of many forms, the skilled one, the most overpowering, the Āptya among the Āptyas. He shatters the seven streams with his might; he overcomes many and matching things.

sanskrit: ni tad dadhiṣe 'varam paraṁ ca yasminn āvithāvasā duroṇe | ā mātarā sthāpayase jigatnū ata inoṣi karvārā purūṇi ||
english: You hold fast both the lower and the upper; in whose house you have protected with your shelter — you establish the two mothers as they come, and from there you dispatch many heroic deeds.

sanskrit: imā brahma bṛhaddivaḥ vivaktīndrāya śūṣam agriyaḥ svarṣāḥ ||
english: These prayers Bṛhaddiva, the foremost, the heaven-winner, proclaims as his praise-shout to Indra.

sanskrit: evā mahān bṛhaddivaḥ atharvo 'vacat svāṁ tanvaṁ indram eva | svasāro mātaribhvarīr ariprā hinvanti ca śavasā vardhayanty ca ||
english: Thus great Bṛhaddiva the Atharvan declared himself to be Indra himself. The stainless sister-winds that breathe on the mother-streams urge him on and increase him with their might.
